stories.headline: Albanese heckled at Sydney mosque over Gaza war stance during Eid prayers
stories.summary: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese was heckled and booed by protesters at Lakemba Mosque on March 20 during Eid al-Fitr prayers, with demonstrators calling him 'genocide supporter' and 'putrid dog' over his government's stance on Israel's offensive in Gaza. Albanese claimed the protest was partly due to his government outlawing extremist organizations like Hizb ut-Tahrir.

stories.headline: RBA raises interest rates to 4.1% in split decision amid inflation concerns
stories.summary: The Reserve Bank of Australia hiked the cash rate by 0.25 percentage points to 4.1% on March 17 in a narrow 5-4 split board decision, citing persistent inflation pressures and the Middle East war's impact on fuel prices. This marked the second consecutive rate rise and brought rates back to their February 2025 level.

stories.headline: Labor wins South Australian election in landslide as One Nation surges past Liberals
stories.summary: South Australian Premier Peter Malinauskas led Labor to a decisive second-term victory on March 21, capturing around 38% of the primary vote. In a historic result, Pauline Hanson's One Nation party achieved its best state result in nearly 30 years with 22% of the primary vote, overtaking the collapsed Liberal Party which fell to just 19%.

stories.headline: AUKUS partnership advances with UK nuclear submarine maintenance and workforce development
stories.summary: The AUKUS agreement progressed with HMS Anson conducting the first UK nuclear submarine maintenance period in Australia, while Western Australia strengthened the partnership through workforce development agreements with UK institutions. The UK also requested up to $1 billion in US support for submarine combat systems.
